analysis: The only change in this file is a comment edit in SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (base lines 4361-4362 became head lines 4361-4363). It clarifies that SSDWriteBehind.consume charges the rate-limit bucket per entry in array order only when the whole donation does not fit. No code, assertions, test logic, crypto, TTL, lookup-tag derivation or storage policy changed. The supplied units (base 3039-4237) are unchanged surrounding test context. I examined that context against T-041 (SSD prefix cache at rest). It exercises existing controls: HMAC-keyed lookup tags, window sidecar tag domain separation, the AAD-bound metadata commitment, fail-closed corrupt-file deletion, per-donation gating, and the queue and byte caps. None of these are weakened. The comment wording could not be checked against SSDWriteBehind.consume itself, since that source was not supplied. That affects documentation accuracy only, not a security conclusion. No new attack surface, no threat-model assumption invalidated, and no threat-model update is needed.
